  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In `augment_files_touched`, `recorded` and `recorded_initial` are filtered copies of the raw `prepush_augmented_paths` marker. When the raw marker is malformed and an issue's module selection fails (`candidates is None`), the restore puts back the filtered entry, so `recorded != original_marker` is still true. That sets `marker_changed=1`, and `--write-back` rewrites the decomposition and reports `written: true`.
  WHY: This breaks the documented no-op contract "Every failure leaves the decomposition unchanged and exits 0", and the new test `test_augment_files_touched_ignored_marker_with_failed_module_is_noop` only covers a well-formed marker. The only content change is that the malformed marker is cleaned up. All four reviewers rated it NIT (mapped to low).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:augment_files_touched, lines 4319-4325 (`recorded_initial` is built from the filtered `recorded` dict), lines 4360-4361 (restore on `candidates is None`), lines 4383-4385 (`original_marker = recorded_raw ...`; `if totals["added"] > 0 or recorded != original_marker:`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The restore brings back the parsed copy of the marker entry, not the raw entry. Three marker shapes trigger it: a non-string list element (e.g. `{"a": ["src/one.py", 5]}`), a non-list value, or a non-dict marker. `validate_decomposition` keeps unknown keys (`data = dict(data)`, line 93). So even when every selection fails, `marker_changed` is set to 1, `${DECOMPOSITION_FILE}` is rewritten and `written: true` is reported.
  WHY: This contradicts the "every failure leaves the decomposition unchanged" statement in the new test and in the agents.d fragment. Only the marker is cleaned up, so `files_touched` and partition results are unaffected.
- HARDENING (scripts/orchestrate_lib.py, augment_files_touched, around line 4385): compute `marker_malformed = recorded_raw is not None and recorded_raw != recorded_initial` once before the loop. Then write back only when `totals["added"] > 0 or recorded != recorded_initial or (marker_malformed and totals["skipped"] < totals["issues"])`. Estimated 2-3 lines; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
- TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE. Every item in issue #8189 is reported as present: the subcommand with its 50-entry cap, the gated wiring, the shared renderer, the tests, and the changelog.d and agents.d fragments.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  WHY: This contradicts "Every failure leaves the decomposition unchanged and exits 0". The content stays correct, but the write should not happen. `test_augment_files_touched_ignored_marker_with_failed_module_is_noop` uses a well-formed marker, so it does not catch this case.

  PROBLEM: `recorded` is a filtered copy of the raw marker, while `original_marker` (line 4383) is the unfiltered raw value. Any dropped content (a non-string key, a non-list value, or a non-string element) makes `recorded != original_marker` permanently true. After a failed selection (`candidates is None`), the restore at lines 4360-4361 puts back the filtered form, so line 4385 sets `marker_changed=1` and `cmd_augment_files_touched` writes back with `written: true`.
  WHY: This contradicts the no-op contract in the agents.d/8189 fragment (line 4). The new test only exercises a well-formed marker. The spurious write also silently drops the malformed marker entries even though every issue was skipped. The reviewer kept it at NIT because the trigger needs malformed model-written JSON.
- HARDENING (scripts/orchestrate_lib.py, augment_files_touched, line 4385): gate the cleaning comparison with `if totals["added"] > 0 or (recorded != original_marker and totals["skipped"] == 0):`. An alternative is to compare against `recorded_initial`. Optionally, add a test case that uses a malformed-element marker with a failing module. Estimated 1 line; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
